summary: This House class models a single house as an object, storing its address, number of bedrooms, and number of bathrooms. The fields are kept private and reached through a constructor plus getter and setter methods, which is the standard shape of a Java domain class.

lines.text: The class acts as a blueprint: each House object created from it holds its own copy of the three fields below.
The street address is text, so String is the natural type. Marking it private means code outside the class cannot touch it directly.
Bedrooms are always counted in whole numbers, so int is the right choice.
Bathrooms use double because real listings describe half baths, and 2.5 cannot be stored in an int.

lines.text: The constructor runs when a house is created with new, and it demands all three values so an object never exists in an incomplete state.
The parameter and the field share the name address, so this.address makes clear that the field is being assigned from the parameter.
A getter hands out the stored value without exposing the field itself, which keeps the class in control of its own data.
A setter lets the address change after the object is built, for example when a typo is corrected.
The return type must match the field's type, so this getter returns a double rather than an int.
